strengths: Strong empirical results: achieves 6.8× higher compression than MiniCache with 2.7% accuracy gains, demonstrating substantial practical improvements on RULER benchmark across multiple models (Llama-3.1, Qwen variants)

Well-motivated approach: compelling analysis showing low token-wise cosine similarity masks well-aligned singular vectors (via CKA), explaining limitations of prior token-similarity-based methods like MiniCache
Practical versatility: post-training method requiring no retraining or architectural changes; works across different attention mechanisms (GQA, MLA), demonstrated on DeepSeek-Coder-V2
Comprehensive experimental evaluation: multiple models tested, standard RULER benchmark with 11 tasks, ablation studies on key/value compression, consistent improvements across group sizes
Clear presentation and sound methodology: well-structured paper with effective visualizations (Figure 2), clear mathematical formulation, and honest discussion of limitations
weaknesses: Critical gap in end-to-end evaluation: paper claims throughput and inference benefits but provides no actual latency/throughput measurements despite on-the-fly SVD and reconstruction overhead; Section 6 acknowledges absence of system integration

Limited technical novelty: applying SVD to concatenated layers is straightforward; cross-layer KV redundancy is known from prior work (CLA, YOCO, LCKV); core contribution is incremental combination of existing techniques

Unjustified design choices: stride-based grouping used despite Figure 2b showing non-uniform CKA alignment; rank selection (1:1.5 key/value ratio) lacks principled justification; no ablation studies on group size sensitivity or rank selection strategy

Narrow baseline comparisons: only compares to MiniCache for inter-layer methods; missing comparisons to recent approaches (LoRC, other compression combinations); Single SVD is authors' own baseline rather than published method

Incomplete experimental analysis: no error bars or statistical significance testing; identified task-dependent compression sweet spots (Section 5.4) are not addressed (fixed 1:1.5 ratio used anyway); limited ablation (Figure 5 uses only 4 RULER tasks); missing sensitivity analyses for rank hyperparameter and group sizes

strengths: Clear empirical analysis of cross-layer singular vector alignment via CKA, effectively motivating the approach with evidence that contradicts prior work assumptions
Practical plug-and-play method requiring no retraining, with simple implementation suitable for existing pretrained models

Comprehensive experimental evaluation across multiple models (Llama-3.1, Qwen2.5, DeepSeek-Coder-V2) and datasets (RULER, RepoBench-P, LCC), including compatibility with emerging architectures like MLA
Strong empirical compression-accuracy trade-offs (6.8× vs MiniCache with +2.7% accuracy improvement; 3× on MLA without degradation)
Generally clear presentation with informative visualizations of cross-layer structure
weaknesses: Critical gap: No end-to-end system evaluation. Paper lacks actual measurements of decoding latency, throughput, or reconstruction cost. Reconstruction requires matrix multiplications (A × Bℓᵢ per layer) that could negate memory savings in bandwidth-bound scenarios. Without this validation, practical impact is unverifiable

Limited technical novelty. The core contribution—concatenating KV-caches and applying SVD instead of per-layer SVD—is straightforward. Stride-based grouping is a simple heuristic without justification. The connection from CKA to compression performance is empirical/intuitive, not rigorously established

Weak theoretical justification. CKA analysis (Appendix A.2) shows correlation with singular vector alignment but not causation for compression optimality. No proof that shared SVD basis is theoretically sound. Eigenvalue analysis (Figure 2c) shown only on NIAH dataset; generalization unclear

Experimental fairness and reproducibility issues: MiniCache re-implemented rather than using official code; code URL marked missing; key implementation details vague (e.g., how was 1:1.5 rank ratio determined?); evaluation limited to 64k context (not tested on 256k/1M where method is designed for)

Unjustified design choices: No ablation on stride-based grouping vs alternatives; fixed rank ratio ignores acknowledged task-dependent sensitivity; no compression of generated tokens justified only by hand-wavy argument; horizontal concatenation not compared to alternatives

Incomplete analysis of when/why method works. High variance across tasks (QA-1 vs QA-2 differ significantly at same compression). Grouping strategy choice (xKV-2 vs xKV-4) shows large performance gap (78.1% vs 87.8%) but is not analyzed. No explanation of failure modes or when not to use method

Missing baselines and comparisons. No comparison with EigenAttention or ShadowKV despite citation; no evaluation against task-aware/context-aware compression methods; Single SVD baseline appears suspiciously weak at high compression without explanation
Scope limitations. Only instruction-tuned models; only long-context scenarios; mainly GQA/MLA architectures (full MHA unclear); all text-based tasks. Generalization to other settings unknown

Methodological inconsistency: Claims 'post-training, fully plug-and-play' but Section 4.1 describes computing SVD 'on the fly during pre-filling' per-request, contradicting post-training nature. Decode-phase reconstruction cost not quantified despite being potentially significant

Practical post-training method requiring no fine-tuning or architectural changes, enabling easy deployment

weaknesses: MiniCache comparison reliability questionable—original code unavailable and had to be re-implemented; catastrophic failure at 1.3× compression seems suspicious despite following official settings

strengths: Novel insight using CKA to diagnose cross-layer singular vector alignment, explaining why prior token-similarity approaches (MiniCache) fail

Training-free, plug-and-play method requiring no retraining or architectural modifications, enabling immediate deployment on existing models

Comprehensive experimental evaluation across multiple models (Llama-3.1, Qwen2.5/3, DeepSeek), benchmarks (RULER, LongBench, NIAH), and diverse baselines, with clear practical wins (8× compression with ≤3% accuracy loss)

Thorough presentation with clear motivation, logical progression, well-designed figures, and extensive ablations (window size, quantization integration, emerging architectures)

strengths: Well-motivated CKA analysis revealing aligned singular vectors despite low token-wise similarity

Training-free, plug-and-play approach applicable to existing pretrained models without retraining

Landmark memory overhead (≈12.5% of original KV at c=8) underexplored; effective compression lower than claimed when accounting for landmarks
Hyperparameter selection unjustified: rank ratio 1:1.5, window size W=4, token budget 2k appear arbitrary with minimal sensitivity analysis
Statistical significance not established: no error bars, confidence intervals, or multiple runs; some differences marginal (88.50% vs 88.80%)

Head-specific sparsity complexity (Eq. 3) not quantified; no ablation comparing head-specific vs. uniform selection

Code availability link is blank (page 1), raising reproducibility concerns

strengths: Novel and well-motivated core insight: CKA analysis reveals aligned singular vectors across layers even when cosine similarity is low, providing a principled departure from prior work like MiniCache

Comprehensive experimental validation across multiple datasets (RULER, LongBench, Multi-turn NIAH), diverse architectures (Llama, Qwen, DeepSeek, GPT-OSS), and thorough baseline comparisons showing consistent improvements
Practical training-free post-hoc method with no architectural modifications required; negligible SVD overhead (3.9% at 128K context) and custom kernel optimizations

Extensive ablation studies including window size analysis, per-layer key/value compression effects, quantization integration, multi-turn robustness, and broader CKA analysis across diverse architectures

Rigorous mathematical framework with clear derivation connecting CKA to aligned singular vectors (Appendix A) and detailed cost analysis (Appendix D.6)

Fixed rank selection across all tasks despite evidence (Figure 6, §D.3) that different tasks have different compression tolerance; acknowledged by authors but no solution proposed, representing missed optimization opportunity

Selective Reconstruction overhead adds complexity: landmark memory overhead (M_lm ≈ NLd/c) is non-negligible, landmark-based selection borrowed from ShadowKV without validation of optimality for cross-layer compression
